value.name: rosa acknowledges what was left
value.description: Rosa tells Asha that what was left to her was kind but not enough for what it meant, while also saying she was left her daughter in a way.
evidence: Rosa looked at her with that long measuring look she had given her at the door on the first day. "It was kind," she said. "It was not enough for what she meant. But she also left me her daughter, in a way, and that is the part that is enough."

value.name: asha files the codicil
value.description: Over the next ten days, Asha formally files the recovered codicil with the register of wills and submits supporting documents.
evidence: They buried the codicil, so to speak, in the proper way, over the next ten days.
Asha filed it with the register of wills.
She submitted Pinsky's notes and Mrs. Adelman's affidavit and a brief explanation of the document's recovery from a place where the testator had directed it to be kept.

value.name: asha conceals burned note
value.description: Asha deliberately omits any mention of a burned note she found in a bathroom sink and decides not to revisit that choice.
evidence: She did not, in her filings, mention a burned note in a bathroom sink.
She thought about it for two nights and then made her decision and did not revisit it.

value.name: daniel declines to contest
value.description: Daniel chooses not to challenge the codicil even though he could have grounds to do so.
evidence: He had grounds, on paper, to make the firm work for the ruling, and Asha had expected, in a corner of her mind, that he would.

value.name: daniel signs codicil acknowledgment
value.description: Daniel meets Asha at her office and signs the papers acknowledging the codicil using her pen.
evidence: He signed the papers acknowledging the codicil.
He sat across from her at her office and signed them with a pen she lent him and he handed the pen back

value.name: daniel explains his decision
value.description: Daniel says he is not signing because he has given up, but because he believes the letter after rereading it.
evidence: "I want you to know I am not signing because I have given up. I am signing because I read the letter twice more after you left, and I believe her."
"That is the better reason," Asha said.

value.name: daniel plans to sell possessions
value.description: Daniel tells Asha he will need to sell some things and that his mother's money will only cover what he must handle if he is careful.
evidence: "I am going to need to sell some things," he said.
"My mother left me money. It is enough to handle what I have to handle if I am careful."
